backlogged.summary: AC-5 handling covers only the evaluator path. A security-reviewer adapter returning adapter_unavailable mid-run is described in SPEC §8 as stopping the run, but no test covers it separately.
In the preflight, `callsCli` skips the check when build and evaluate/runAdapter are injected. That is test-only plumbing, and it adds a condition to the run entry point.

authStatus treats a settings.json that parses to a non-object, such as `null` or `[]`, as 'not authenticated' with the generic reason. That is acceptable, but it is not distinguished from an absent file.
verify.test_count is not configured, so a decrease in test count is not checked.

For gemini exit codes other than 41 (and for other adapters), runAdapter still puts tail(stderr) into detail as exit_nonzero. If a CLI echoes a credential on some other failure, that text can end up in the run report or verdict. This behaviour existed before F20 and SC-1 only covers the auth decision, so it is not blocking; redacting known auth-variable values from the detail would be a hardening follow-up.

authStatus trusts any non-empty GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI / GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_GCA value, including 'false'. That can report 'authenticated' when gemini will actually fail with exit 41. The run then blocks with adapter_unavailable (AC-5), so it fails safe, but the preflight passes when it should not.

Preflight is skipped when both build and evaluate/runAdapter are injected without diagnose. This only affects tests, but a future caller that injects only one of them without diagnose would silently skip the preflight.
